subject: Support playbook: intake + severity mapping for Runtime LTS backport requests
body:
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Owen Phillips <owen.phillips@redwoodinference.com>, Hanae Suzuki <hanae.suzuki@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Support playbook: intake + severity mapping for Runtime LTS backport requests

Connor — looping you in on the Support-side playbook draft for LTS backport requests.

Goal: when an enterprise customer asks for “can you backport X to runtime-1.18-lts”, Support can (1) capture the right diagnostics up front, (2) map severity consistently (Sev1/Sev2/Security), and (3) route to Release Eng/Runtime with enough context to make a fast go/no-go.

Draft (Confluence): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/x/lts-support-playbook-draft

Asks:
1) Please confirm the severity mapping aligns with the LTS backport rubric you’re standardizing.
2) Please confirm the minimum diagnostics list is workable (not too heavy, but enough to reproduce / perf-validate).
3) For Security: do we want Support to route via Hanae/Sec response first, or straight to you + Hanae in parallel?

Attachments (what Support will use in tickets):
- LTS_Backport_Request_Template_v3.docx
- Severity_Mapping_LTS_Backports_v2.pdf

---

Proposed intake: (Support creates/updates SUP ticket + internal LTS Backport Request stub)
Required fields:
- Customer + environment: Hosted / Dedicated / Private (VPC/on-prem), region, deployment size (GPU type/count), autoscaling settings (if Dedicated)
- Runtime: exact runtime tag (e.g., 1.18.1-lts), build hash if Private, installer/helm version
- Model(s): model ID + quantization profile + context length distribution (if known)
- Symptom category: crash / correctness / latency / throughput / memory leak / scheduler behavior
- Business impact: user-facing outage? degradation %? volume affected? deadlines (e.g., regulatory change-control window)
- Repro: minimal prompt / request payload where possible; otherwise request IDs + timestamps
- Logs + traces: runtime logs, scheduler logs, OOM traces, kernel errors; correlation/request IDs
- Perf evidence (if perf regression): before/after p50/p95, tokens/sec, prompt/completion sizes, concurrency
- Mitigations tried: rollback, pinning, feature flags, config overrides

Proposed routing:
- Sev1 crash / data integrity: page Release Eng on-call + Runtime triage; target initial response within 4 business hours
- Sev2 degradation: file + triage in next business day; can be batched into next patch window
- Security: treat as out-of-band candidate; follow vuln response workflow (Hanae)

Thanks,
Dev

—
Dev Patel
Support Workflow Owner
Redwood Inference



From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Owen Phillips <owen.phillips@redwoodinference.com>, Hanae Suzuki <hanae.suzuki@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 10:04 AM PST
Subject: Re: Support playbook: intake + severity mapping for Runtime LTS backport requests

This looks on the right track.

On your questions:

1) Severity mapping
- Please explicitly tie Sev1/Sev2 to “backport eligibility” so Support doesn’t implicitly promise a backport.
  * Eligible by default: Security, Sev1 crash, Sev1 correctness (wrong output due to runtime bug), Sev1 scheduler starvation causing effective outage.
  * Eligible with higher bar: Sev2 regressions (latency/throughput) if impact is broad + reproducible + mitigation not viable.
  * Not eligible: feature requests, perf micro-optimizations, changes that touch kernel autotune/scheduling heuristics unless the bug is in LTS-only behavior.

2) Minimum diagnostics
- Strong yes on requiring exact runtime tag + deployment packaging version. We’ve already burned time on “1.18-ish” reports.
- For perf regressions: the biggest missing item is a “known-good reference”: either the prior LTS patch or last mainline version they were stable on. Add that as required.
- Request IDs + timestamps are enough when we can pull traces, but for Private we can’t. For Private, push for an on-box bundle (logs + config + version output).

3) Security routing
- Route in parallel: Support opens SUP + tags “security” + pings Hanae + me. We’ll decide if it becomes an out-of-band LTS patch.

One more: add a “Customer communication guardrails” section:
- Support should say “we’ll evaluate for LTS backport per policy” (not “we will backport”).
- Provide target timelines as ranges (triage vs fix vs patch availability).

If you update the doc accordingly, I’m comfortable with this being the template we use for pilot.

Connor

—
Connor O’Brien
Release Engineering Lead (Runtime LTS)
Redwood Inference



From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, Owen Phillips <owen.phillips@redwoodinference.com>, Hanae Suzuki <hanae.suzuki@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 10:23 AM PST
Subject: Re: Support playbook: intake + severity mapping for Runtime LTS backport requests

Adding CS angle (pilot accounts): customers are going to ask for “status” frequently during triage.

Can we include in the playbook:
- A short status ladder Support/CS can use:
  1) Intake complete (awaiting logs)
  2) Reproduced internally
  3) Candidate fix identified (pending risk review)
  4) Approved for LTS backport (target patch window)
  5) Patch available (upgrade/rollback guidance)
- And who owns customer-facing updates at each stage (Support vs CS vs Release Eng).

Also suggest a standard line for change control-heavy customers:
- “If a backport is approved, we can provide signed artifacts + checksums + release notes; availability depends on perf gates and required approvals.”

Thanks,
Rachel

—
Rachel Kim
Enterprise CS Lead (LTS Pilot)
Redwood Inference

Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Owen Phillips <owen.phillips@redwoodinference.com>, Hanae Suzuki <hanae.suzuki@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 11:01 AM PST
Subject: Re: Support playbook: intake + severity mapping for Runtime LTS backport requests

+1 to all.

Two practical notes from Support queue:

1) We should explicitly list what to ask for when the symptom is “latency regression” (we keep getting screenshots).
Suggested required checklist:
- p50/p95 end-to-end latency AND time-to-first-token (TTFT)
- concurrency level (avg + peak), QPS, prompt/completion tokens
- affected routes (chat/completions/embeddings) and whether streaming is enabled
- customer-side timeouts/retries settings

2) Ticket labeling / routing
- Add: “LTS-Backport-Request” label + “runtime-lts” component
- Add: “needs-diagnostics” state so we can pause without losing SLA visibility

If you want, I can add these sections into the Confluence draft this afternoon.

Jasmine

—
Jasmine Liu
Customer Support (Enterprise)
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 12:06 PM PST
Subject: Re: Support playbook: intake + severity mapping for Runtime LTS backport requests

Adding a “crash/correctness” diagnostics block (this is usually where we get stuck):

Crash / OOM / deadlock required:
- full stack trace (or core dump pointer if they have it) + last 5 minutes of runtime logs
- GPU memory stats at time of incident (nvidia-smi output if Private)
- exact model + batch size + max tokens + context length, plus whether speculative decoding / caching is enabled
- if scheduler-related: queue depth, backpressure/load-shedding settings, number of workers

Correctness required:
- minimal repro prompt + expected vs actual output (with random seed if supported)
- confirmation whether they see it on a different region/GPU type
- if it’s structured output/tool calling: schema + example failing response

Also: for any backport request, require “customer can validate” contact + their validation plan (what will they run to confirm fix). This helps avoid the loop of shipping a patch they can’t verify.

Owen

—
Owen Phillips
Support Escalation Engineer
Redwood Inference



From: Hanae Suzuki <hanae.suzuki@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 1:18 PM PST
Subject: Re: Support playbook: intake + severity mapping for Runtime LTS backport requests

On Security routing:

- Please add a section: “If customer claims vulnerability/exploit, do NOT request repro details in email.”
  * Keep details in SUP ticket restricted + Security channel.
  * Collect high-level: impacted versions, environment, whether they have indicators of compromise.

- For LTS security backports, we’ll usually need:
  * CVE (if assigned) or internal tracking ID
  * affected component (runtime / deps / container base image)
  * whether customer requires SBOM/provenance attestation

Parallel triage is fine: tag me + Connor + “security” label.

Hanae

—
Hanae Suzuki
Vulnerability Response Coordination
Redwood Inference



From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 2:46 PM PST
Subject: Re: Support playbook: intake + severity mapping for Runtime LTS backport requests

Thanks all — I updated the Confluence draft with:
- Eligibility guardrails (“evaluate per policy”, not a promise)
- Required “known-good reference version” for perf regressions
- Private-specific “support bundle” request (logs + config + version output)
- Customer status ladder + ownership (Support/CS/Release Eng)
- Ticket labels/states (“LTS-Backport-Request”, “needs-diagnostics”, “runtime-lts”)
- Security handling note (no sensitive repro details over email; route restricted)

Updated draft: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/x/lts-support-playbook-draft

Open items (need your quick yes/no):
1) Triage targets to publish internally:
   - Sev1: initial response <= 4 business hours; backport decision target 2 business days (assuming repro)
   - Sev2: decision target 5 business days
   - Security: per vuln response; out-of-band possible
2) Should Support open a separate internal “LTS Backport” tracking ticket, or keep it inside SUP with labels + a linked ENG task created by Release Eng?

If I get confirmation today, I’ll roll this into the Support handbook and we’ll start using it for incoming pilot tickets (SUP-18544 is the first one that will use the new template).

Dev

—
Dev Patel
Support Workflow Owner
Redwood Inference
